role: Spec of the NgRx facade of a feature slice.

describedBy.text: The store mock is `const storeMock: Partial<Store> = { dispatch: jest.fn(), selectSignal: jest.fn(() => signal(null)), select: jest.fn(() => of(null)) }`; setup is `MockBuilder(Facade).mock(Store, storeMock)` in `beforeAll` and `facade = MockRender(Facade).point.componentInstance`.

Every feature area keeps the canonical layout: `data-access/+state/` (the view's `<name>.store.ts` signal store and, only for data several independent views share, an NgRx slice - actions, reducer, selectors, effects, facade - each with `tests/`), `data-access/services/` (HTTP only), `models/{consts,enums,interfaces,types}` with an `index.ts` barrel, `shared/{utils,guards,pipes,directives[,routes]}` each with `tests/`, plus `shared/mocks/` for the spec fixtures several specs share, `components-<area>/{feature,ui}/`, and for multi-step wizards a `shell/<area>-shell.routes.ts`. HTTP interceptors are app-level, never inside an area.

items.text: The store mock is `const storeMock: Partial<Store> = { dispatch: jest.fn(), selectSignal: jest.fn(() => signal(null)), select: jest.fn(() => of(null)) }`; setup is `MockBuilder(Facade).mock(Store, storeMock)` in `beforeAll` and `facade = MockRender(Facade).point.componentInstance`.
One flat `it` per public method at the top `describe` level (no nested `describe`s for a proxy class).
Every assertion is `expect(storeMock.dispatch).toHaveBeenCalledWith(actions.x({ ...exact payload }))` — never a bare `toHaveBeenCalled()` (it would pass for the wrong action).
Methods with nullable parameters have two tests: a concrete value and `null`.
No-payload methods assert `actions.x()`; multi-argument methods assert the full positional-argument→payload-field mapping.
Array/complex payloads use complete domain fixtures; `{} as X` casts are acceptable (the facade never reads payload fields).
Signals are not tested (the mock returns `signal(null)`; selector logic has its own spec, component behavior mocks the facade); no `expect.objectContaining`/`expect.any`.
`afterEach` runs `jest.clearAllMocks()` (otherwise the null-branch assertion sees the previous call).

A method that waits through the shared wait-until-effect-completes service asserts the exact action-creator pair it waits on (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(actions.addUserSuccess, actions.addUserFail)`) - a bare `toHaveBeenCalled()` passes when the facade waits on the wrong operation, the one real bug such a method can have.

items.text: Specs live in a `tests/` folder next to the code under test; snapshots in `tests/__snapshots__/`.
Stack is Jest + ng-mocks; suites sharing a fixture/TestBed use `ngMocks.faster()` with setup in `beforeAll`.

`afterEach` restores all shared state: `jest.clearAllMocks()`, every signal mutated inside tests reset to its initial value, selector overrides reset; data (re)established in `beforeEach` is reset in `beforeEach`, not undone in `afterEach`.

Variables holding an injected dependency (mock, spy, `TestBed.inject(...)` result) use the full descriptive name derived from the dependency type (keeping the feature/area part of the class name), never shortened to a generic role name.

A dependency mock/stub is checked against the real contract instead of cast into it: `satisfies SomeService` for a full stub, `satisfies Partial<SomeService>` or an annotated `Partial<SomeService>` for the deliberate subsets the facade, component and guard test instructions prescribe — never `as SomeService`, which silences every drift between the mock and the contract it stands for.

Test-loop data is passed directly: `it.each` / `describe.each` / `test.each` receives its rows as an array literal written inside the call, and each row keeps its values as literals in place — never a named dataset const passed to `it.each(dataset)`, and never per-case variables (fixtures, inputs, expected values) declared above and referenced from the rows. Rows that repeat a value write it out again; the no-duplicated-test-data rule below never pulls data out of a dataset row.

Every `describe` title is either the exact code identifier under test — matching its real casing (`describe('myFunction')`, `describe('UserPanelFacade')`) — or a descriptive phrase whose first word is capitalized (`describe('Tests for myFunction')`); a descriptive title never starts with a lowercase word (`describe('tests for myFunction')`).

probe.message: tytuł `describe` to opis zaczynający się małą literą

items.text: Every `it` description starts with `should` and states the expected behavior (e.g. `it('should return an empty list when the request fails')`); `it.each` description templates follow the same rule.
Fixtures are complete objects of their domain type; `{} as X` is acceptable only when the code under test never reads the payload's fields.

The same test data is never duplicated across cases: define a shared object/dataset once - typed with the real interface (`const baseUser: User = {...}`), at the nearest `describe` the tests share - and reuse it directly when the data is identical, or derive near-identical variants from it with the spread operator (`{ ...baseFixture, changedField: value }`), however few fields differ - never hand-write a second copy of an equivalent literal. A literal value several fixtures or payloads share (an id, a name) is one const referenced everywhere.
No existence-only tests — never `it('should be created', () => expect(x).toBeTruthy())` or `toBeDefined()`-style assertions (zero diagnostic value).

Any spy or mock called with arguments is asserted on those arguments with `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` (or `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(...)` for effect-driven repeats) — a bare `toHaveBeenCalled()`/`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` that ignores the payload is insufficient; `toHaveBeenCalled()` is reserved for genuinely argument-less calls. Such a call is never asserted with an empty `toHaveBeenCalledWith()`.

Every `subscribe(...)` opened in a spec is bounded with a `take(...)` operator (`take(1)` for a single expected emission, `take(n)`/`bufferCount(n)` when a known number is expected) so it completes and cannot leak into later tests.

No forced casts to satisfy the type checker: no `as unknown as X`, `as never` or `as undefined as never`, and no double cast where a single `as X` suffices - a mock or fixture is typed properly (`Partial<X>` + `satisfies`) instead; no indexed-access type annotation where the type has a name.
Behavior-bearing code follows TDD: a failing test first (failing for the expected reason), then the minimal implementation, then refactor with tests green.

items.text: After changing any source file, its spec is run and green before commit (the pre-commit hook lints but does not run tests).

A `describe` groups related tests: a spec of a single method keeps its `it`s at the top level, never wrapped in a `describe` of their own, unless an item of the file's own instruction asks for one `describe` per function or per effect.
subject: describe\s*\(

items.text: A fixture or builder a second spec of the area needs is moved to `<area>/shared/mocks/<name>.mock.ts`, exported as `<name>Mock`, typed with the real interface and imported by its concrete path from every spec - never copied into each spec. Test-loop rows stay inline in their `it.each` calls (the test-loop item above).
A `done` callback is typed - `(done: () => void)` or `(done: jest.DoneCallback)` - never a bare `(done)`.
subject: \bdone\b

items.text: One `it` verifies one behaviour: a test that triggers two independent actions or asserts two unrelated outcomes is split into two `it`s, each title naming its own behaviour - one failure then says which behaviour broke.

Names are full and descriptive — no abbreviations and no one-letter identifiers; shortening is allowed only for well-established abbreviations or when the full name would exceed ~25–30 characters or 4–5 words.
items.okEvidence: linia każdej deklaracji, której nazwę sprawdziłeś (L3, L7, L12), nie zakres pliku

items.text: No unnecessary type assertions (`as`), especially `as never` and assertions on primitive types; use a single `as Type` only when the compiler requires it; `as unknown as Type` only when the compiler/ESLint rejects a single assertion because of an incompatible shape.

No type annotation through indexed access (`const disks: PoolLayout['disks']`): use the named type (`PoolLayoutDisk[]`) or let inference type the value; indexed access stays only where the property's type has no name of its own.

A rename is complete: every name the change renames - a file or folder, an exported symbol, a class or store member, an input or output, a component/directive selector or pipe name, an action, a selector, a route path, a CSS class, a `data-test` value, an enum member, a translation key - has no use of its old name left anywhere in the repository: code, templates, styles, specs, mocks, snapshots, e2e tests, routes, barrels, configs and the base-language translation file (`en.json`), where a renamed key is renamed as well. The other locale files are the one exception: they are never touched (i18n#1), so the old key path they keep is no leftover. Whoever renames dispatches a fresh verification sub-agent once the rename is written (Agent tool, `general-purpose`): its prompt lists every old and new name and the repository root; it searches the whole tree but the other locale files for every old name - whole words, string literals, dotted translation-key paths and the key's leaf inside the nested `en.json` - and replies with each leftover `path:line`; every leftover is fixed and the sub-agent runs again until it finds none (a session without the Agent tool makes the same search itself and says so). A review judges the result only: an old name still in use is a finding at the renamed line, naming every leftover `path:line`.

A boolean - a field, signal, input, variable or a method returning a flag - is named with a predicate prefix that reads as a yes/no question (`isActive`, `hasChildren`, `canEdit`, `shouldRetry`; loading flags `isLoading<X>`), never a bare noun or adjective (`active`, `loading`, `children`). The fields of an API interface keep the names the API sends.

items.text: A comment explains only what the code cannot say itself - a non-obvious why, a tricky edge case, a workaround, a subtle gotcha; a comment restating what the code does or narrating obvious steps is a finding, and a clearer name replaces it. The section comments of a models barrel and the justification of a suppression comment are required, not this item's.
One import declaration per module specifier: two `import` statements from the same path (`../../../models` twice) are merged into one.

instructions.name: Angular & TypeScript best practices
preamble: This instruction OWNS the framework-level API rules: typing, the signals API, DI, standalone declarables, host bindings, lazy routes, the forms pattern and RxJS usage. File placement and template rules belong to the component and component-template instructions; rendering cost and change detection to the performance instruction; WCAG 2.2 level AA — which new or changed UI must satisfy — to the accessibility instruction, which owns every accessibility finding. A violation is reported ONCE, under the most specific instruction covering it.

items.text: Strict typing everywhere: no `any` (use `unknown` plus narrowing when the shape is genuinely uncertain); prefer inference where the type is obvious; exported functions and service methods declare their parameter and return types. A signal input or output carries a type argument only when its default cannot express the type - `input.required<T>()`, `output<T>()`, `input<Item[]>([])`, `input<string | null>(null)` - never one its default already infers (`input(0)`, `input(false)`, `signal('')`, not `input<number>(0)`).

probe.message: argument typu powtarza typ, który wartość domyślna już wyznacza

items.text: Type annotations earn their place: annotate where inference is absent or wrong — an empty literal (`const items: Item[] = []`, `signal<Item[]>([])`), a `null`/`undefined` seed, an object literal assembled field-by-field against a domain interface, and the parameters plus return type of every exported function, service method and util. Never annotate what the call already types (`inject()`, `input(<default>)`, `signal()`/`computed()`/`toSignal()`, `_fb.nonNullable.group(...)`, `createSelector(...)`, `as const`, any variable initialized from a typed call) — a redundant annotation is boilerplate under the code-quality instruction. A view-model object a component or mapper builds for the template with fields of its own (a row extended with a tooltip, a disabled reason, a label) is typed by a named interface in `models/`, never left as an inferred object literal nobody declared.

A suppression comment added by the diff (`@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `eslint-disable*`) carries a one-line justification and the narrowest scope that works (line-level over file-level); `@ts-expect-error` is used wherever it compiles, because it fails once the underlying problem is fixed. The `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/member-ordering */` allowed by the effects instruction is the one standing exception.
RxJS operators and creation functions are imported from `'rxjs'` - never from the deprecated `'rxjs/operators'` entry point, however much legacy code still imports it.
subject: rxjs/operators

instructions.name: Code quality — duplication, dead code, boilerplate & consistency
preamble: The two duplication items (the first two below) are reported with severity 🔴 **High**, every other violation of this checklist with 🟡 **Medium** — never softened because it looks cosmetic and never raised because it looks dangerous.

This instruction OWNS duplication, dead/unnecessary code, boilerplate and inconsistency: when another instruction or the cross-file pass covers the same occurrence (the architecture "reuse before creating" rule, the duplication-drift and naming-consistency questions, a jscpd candidate from the context), the occurrence is reported ONCE — here, with the severity above.

Scope is the skill's scope gate: the finding is anchored on a line the diff touched. A copy that the diff ADDS of pre-existing code is a finding (anchored on the new copy) once the code exists three or more times; duplication, dead code or inconsistency living entirely in untouched lines is not.

items.text: No duplicated logic: the same expression, condition, transformation, mapping, validator set, literal/const value or markup fragment appearing three or more times — in one file, across the files of this diff, or re-implemented next to an existing shared util, component, builder, model or i18n key, which counts as one of the copies (look for them with the Grep tool over the target's `snapshotDir`, the reviewed revision exported for this run, or with its `commands.grep` when it has none). Two occurrences are not a finding under this item. Test data a spec repeats in its own cases (fixture objects, the same literal in several cases) is unit-tests#12's, never this item's; logic a spec repeats stays here. Report every copy at the place that should reuse instead of repeat, and name the other copies. A function or expression shorter than 5 lines whose logic is simple - a single filter, map, find, some/every or sort over its input, or a property pick - is not duplicated logic under this item, however often it repeats: it is never reported as code to extract into a reusable util (utils#9).
items.secondQuestion: Które wyrażenia, pola, mapowania i literały tego pliku wyszukano w pozostałych plikach (stan, szablony, utils, modele, i18n) i z jakim wynikiem?

items.text: No copy-paste-with-a-tweak: three or more near-identical blocks differing only in a value, a field name or one branch become one parameterized function, const or loop — this includes near-identical test fixtures, mock objects and `it` bodies (which belong in an `it.each` dataset). Two such blocks are not a finding under this item.
items.okEvidence: pierwsza linia każdego z porównanych bloków (L12, L30, L48), nie zakres obejmujący je wszystkie

items.text: No unused code: unused imports, variables, consts, parameters, private fields and methods, unreachable statements, dead branches, exported symbols with no consumer left in the repo, inputs/outputs nothing binds, and leftovers of an earlier iteration of this very change. This includes a public store, facade or service member (a field, a signal, a selector exposed through a facade, a method) that nothing in the repository reads, and a parameter every caller passes the same constant (`null`, `undefined`, `false`) - it is dropped, or given that value as its default.

No unnecessary code: a wrapper that only forwards to the wrapped call, a variable used once on the very next line, `else` after a `return`, a condition that can never be false, `?.`/`??`/`try` guarding a value the types already guarantee, a hand-written helper an existing shared function already provides, an abstraction (interface, base class, generic, options object) introduced for a single consumer "for the future".

No boilerplate: empty or pass-through lifecycle hooks and constructors, getters/methods that only return a field, scaffolding and generator leftovers (sample fields, `TODO` stubs nothing tracks), values re-declared although the framework already defaults to them, and ceremony that adds no behavior.

Code is consistent with its surroundings: one concept keeps one name everywhere (and one name never denotes two concepts), sibling cases are solved the same way (same guard style, same mapping approach, same error handling, same async style), related functions keep the same parameter order and return shape, and members keep the file's established ordering. Code that answers an already-answered question differently is a finding at the new location. A name that merely breaks a naming convention (casing, abbreviation) is not this rule — it is a finding only under the instruction that sets that convention. An inconsistency is a finding only when each variant is valid by itself; when a variant breaks another item, that item's finding is the one reported.

A property chain repeated three times or more in one function or test (`component.form.controls.x`, `fixture.componentInstance.y`) is destructured once at its top (`const { labelMethod, capacity } = component.form.controls;`).

instructions.name: Test coverage — untested cases & edge cases
instructions.gate: the file carries behaviour a spec could execute - a function or class method with a body (however trivial - a one-line setter or a lone .next() call is behaviour), a branch, handler or effect - not only declarations, re-exports or route/config literals
preamble: This instruction OWNS coverage gaps — which behavioral cases, branches, edge cases and state permutations the diff leaves untested; every finding here is 🔵 **Missing Unit Test**. The unit-tests instruction owns the SHAPE of a spec (location, setup, naming, assertion style). A gap is reported ONCE, here — never also as a unit-tests finding. The items below are facets of one requirement — the file's behaviour is tested — so everything a file breaks here is ONE finding: its Problem lists each untested case with its line, and its Reguła names every item it breaks. A file with no spec at all leaves its branches, failure paths and edge cases untested too: those items are broken, not passed, and that one finding names them.

items.text: Do not assume coverage from the spec's mere existence — enumerate the behavioral cases the changed lines introduce and cross-check each one against the spec's actual test cases.
items.okEvidence: linia każdego zmienionego zachowania i ścieżka spec z liniami przypadków, które je sprawdzają, nie zakres pliku

items.text: Every conditional branch introduced or modified by the diff is tested for BOTH outcomes: each `if`/`else`, ternary, `switch` case (including `default`), guard clause, early return and short-circuit path (`&&`, `||`, `??`, `?.`).
Every failure path is tested, not only the happy path: rejected promises, erroring observables/HTTP calls, thrown exceptions, `catch`/`catchError` blocks, timeout/retry logic and fallback values.

Edge cases of the data the changed code reads are covered: empty array/collection, `null`/`undefined` input, empty string, `0` and negative numbers, boundary values of every comparison (test the exact limit of `<` vs `<=`), first/last element handling, duplicates where uniqueness matters.

State permutations are covered: every boolean/loading/error flag the changed code reads is exercised in its non-default state as well as its default, and each flag is asserted independently so a single flag flipping the result is caught.
Public API surface changed by the diff (new method, new input/output, new selector/action handling) has at least one test exercising it through that public surface, not only through internals.
